column3: The immediate siege context recalls their covenant not to turn their backs, directly framing steadfast fulfillment.
Treating God's covenant and oaths as a small bargain supplies a contrary image of covenant betrayal.

Repeatedly casting aside a covenant gives a clear contrary pattern to believers who do not alter theirs.

The rejected parallel concerning a messenger being a man does not clarify covenantal truthfulness.
Its division between belief and turning away offers only a broad contrast to the believers named in the focus.

That prior messengers were men is not evidence for the focus's covenantal description of believers.

It explicitly commands fulfillment of God's covenant and forbids breaking confirmed oaths.

Submission to God's and the messenger's settled command gives a close same-surah posture of faithful obedience.

The command to consider human creation has no material connection to the focus.
Completion of Zayd's marital matter gives only a lexical and general completion parallel.

Witnessing a dying person does not clarify covenantal waiting.
Testing distinguishes those who proved true from liars, directly sharpening truthfulness under pressure.

Its warning to believe in a confirming revelation does not add to the focus's covenantal fidelity.

Satan's expectation becoming true through followers is not the focus's truthfulness or pledge-keeping.

Exchanging God's favor for disbelief gives a distant contrary to retaining one's commitment unchanged.

It makes continued treaty obligation depend on reciprocal uprightness, adding a concrete rule of covenant fidelity.
Truthful and lying claimants are to be distinguished before permission is granted, giving an applied truthfulness test.
Its rules of prophetic priority and kinship do not clarify the focus's covenantal faithfulness.
It defines true believers by unwavering faith and striving with wealth and selves, a close enacted measure of truthfulness.
Mutual waiting is a watchful challenge between opponents, only loosely related to the focus's waiting believers.
God's promise of succession, established religion, and security to believing doers gives a broader fulfillment horizon.
Reviewing what one's hands sent ahead is not a parallel to waiting faithfully for one's term.

The prohibition on exchanging wives is a distinct domestic use of replacement language.

Its protection of unknown believing men and women is not about their covenant or its fulfillment.

The choice offered to the Prophet's wives does not add to the focus's contrast of completion and waiting.

Men on the elevations awaiting entry into the Garden do not illuminate the focus's fulfilled pledge.

God's decisive execution of a command is only a general parallel to completion of a term.

Musa's appointment and request to see his Lord do not clarify fulfillment, waiting, or non-alteration.

God's guardianship and power over resurrection do not add to the focus's pledge pattern.

The assurance of forgiveness does not specify covenant fulfillment or steadfast waiting.
Changing the commanded word and receiving punishment supplies a distant contrary to remaining unaltered.
Household visitation etiquette does not add to the focus's covenantal distinctions.
Recognition that the Merciful's promise and the messengers proved true repeats the earlier promise-truth theme.

Those with prophets remain steadfast through great hardship and do not weaken or submit, closely matching fidelity under pressure.
The living status of those killed in God's way provides a close horizon for believers who have completed their term.
Believers who respond after injury and retain goodness and taqwa give a direct battle-pressure model of steadfast faith.
Threats increase the believers in faith and reliance rather than causing retreat, paralleling the focus's siege setting.
The commands to persevere, endure, remain stationed, and fear God supply a broad discipline of steadfast waiting.
The command to fulfill all binding commitments directly supports the focus's fulfilled covenant with God.

God's covenant with the Children of Israel, tied to sustained duties, provides a structured covenant-performance parallel.

The command to fulfill God's covenant reinforces the focus's account of believers who did not alter theirs.
The prohibition against betraying God, the messenger, and entrusted duties gives the direct contrary to covenant fidelity.
Believers facing an opposing force are commanded to stand firm and remember God, closely fitting the siege context.
Obedience, unity, and patience are required so that strength is not lost, supplying practical content for steadfastness.
Completing a treaty through its stated term gives a direct temporal model for honoring a binding commitment.
Those who break oaths and initiate aggression form a concrete contrary to faithful covenant-keeping.
True believers do not seek exemption from striving with wealth and lives, distinguishing committed action from withdrawal.
Believers are commanded to fear God and remain with the truthful, directly reinforcing the focus's defining quality.
Believers are not to remain behind the messenger, giving a close battle-pressure counterpart to loyal endurance.
The warning not to unravel confirmed oaths after making them firm directly clarifies the focus's non-alteration.
The explicit command to fulfill every covenant directly supports the focus's faithful believers.
Ismail is described as true to his promise, providing a focused prophetic model of enacted fidelity.
The successful believers are explicitly those who observe their trusts and covenants.
The arrival of the confederate forces establishes the immediate pressure under which the focus's faithfulness appears.
The siege's fear and shaken hearts describe the trial that distinguishes the faithful from those who turn back.
It explicitly states that the believers were tested and violently shaken immediately before the focus's steadfast response.
The hypocrites' claim that God's promise was delusive supplies the immediate contrary to believers who attest its truth.
Flight cannot avert death or killing, sharpening the focus's distinction between fulfilled terms and continued waiting.
Its denial of any protector from God provides only broad siege context for remaining faithful.
Those who hinder others from fighting form a local contrary to believers who honor their commitment under pressure.
Their fear, avarice, and hostile speech extend the local portrait of those unlike the steadfast believers.
Their expectation of the confederates' return shows persistent fear, a limited contrary to the focus's resolve.
Messengers who convey God's messages and fear none but Him provide a close model of unaltered duty under pressure.
Ibrahim's readiness to carry out the vision with his son gives a concentrated model of completing a divinely binding command.
Those who say their Lord is God and then remain steadfast directly express sustained, unaltered commitment.
The command to remain upright as commanded reinforces continuity of divinely directed commitment.
Those who affirm God as Lord and then remain steadfast closely parallel the focus's enduring believers.
Divine testing identifies those who strive and remain patient, clarifying how faithful commitment is disclosed.
The pledge to the messenger is declared a pledge to God, giving an explicit covenantal counterpart to the focus.
God's approval of believers who pledged under the tree directly connects covenant, pressure, and faithful hearts.
Believers in God and His messengers are called the truthful, extending the focus's identity of true believers.
The rebuke of saying what one does not do supplies the direct contrary to truthfulness embodied in action.
God's strong disapproval of words not enacted reinforces the focus's lived fulfillment rather than mere assertion.
The believers who faithfully observe their trusts and covenants provide a direct parallel to the focus.
